2610.37434.title: FeatureArc: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Evolving Features
2610.37434.authors: Yunlong Wang , Alyssa Wu , Cuiyun Gao , Jia Feng , Songyuanyi Lu , Zhichao Hu
2610.37434.abstract_en: A software feature usually evolves over time: developers extend its first version as new use cases and requirements arrive, and each extension builds on code written earlier. Most feature benchmarks evaluate a single request on a fixed codebase. Feature evolution requires evaluating successive extensions on an agent's own earlier code and checking whether the feature remains correct. We introduce FeatureArc to evaluate coding agents on evolving features, together with a pipeline that constructs its tasks from repository histories. The benchmark combines dependencies between successive stages of the same feature, explicit requirements and interface contracts, and executable checks across four programming languages. The pipeline validates fail-to-pass (F2P) tests for new behavior and pass-to-pass (P2P) tests for existing behavior on the reference code before and after each stage. We evaluated 10 coding agents on 73 manually reviewed tasks of 2 to 10 stages. Each agent works in one persistent session and workspace without external test feedback or rollback. The evaluation reveals a gap between first-stage and whole-feature success: pooled success falls from 62.7% at the first stage to 28.5% when the whole feature is tested on the final code. Trajectory analysis identifies inherited defects as a common failure mechanism, present in 72.9% of failed later stages. These earlier errors often remain undetected: in stages following a failure, agents leave the earlier error unnoticed about 95% of the time, and their self-tests rarely revisit earlier stages. Evolving a feature autonomously, without human checks between stages, therefore remains a substantial challenge for current coding agents. At Tencent, the pipeline extends internal evaluations to this setting and guides the development of Hunyuan, Tencent's family of large language models.
2610.37434.affiliation: Hunyuan Team, Tencent; The Chinese University of Hong Kong
2610.37434.update_target: Evaluation of successive feature edits on the agent’s own persistent code
2610.37434.mechanism_en: History-derived stage contracts and executable F2P/P2P checks test new behavior and preservation. One session/workspace continues without external test feedback or rollback.
2610.37434.result_en: Across 73 reviewed tasks and ten agents, pooled success falls 62.7%→28.5% from first stage to final whole-feature correctness; inherited defects appear in 72.9% of failed later stages.
2610.37434.boundary_en: Feature/code evolution is not itself agent learning. The no-feedback/no-rollback protocol and persistent errors explain a specific evaluation boundary, not every software-development workflow.
2610.37434.abstract_zh: 软件功能通常随时间演变：开发者随着新用例和需求出现，扩展其首个版本，每次扩展都基于此前写出的代码。多数功能基准在固定代码库上评估单个请求。功能演化需要在智能体自己的早期代码上评估连续扩展，并检查功能是否保持正确。我们提出 FeatureArc 来评估编码智能体处理持续演化功能的能力，并提供从仓库历史构建任务的流水线。基准结合了同一功能连续阶段间的依赖、显式要求与接口契约，以及跨四种编程语言的可执行检查。流水线在参考代码每个阶段前后，验证新行为的失败到通过（F2P）测试，以及既有行为的通过到通过（P2P）测试。我们在 73 个人工审阅任务上评估 10 个编码智能体，每项任务含 2—10 个阶段。每个智能体都在单个持久会话和工作区中工作，没有外部测试反馈或回滚。评估揭示首阶段与完整功能成功率之间的差距：汇总成功率从首阶段的 62.7%，降至在最终代码上测试完整功能时的 28.5%。轨迹分析识别出继承缺陷这一常见失败机制，存在于 72.9% 的失败后续阶段。这些早期错误往往未被发现：在失败之后的阶段，智能体约 95% 的时候未注意到先前错误，自测也很少回查早期阶段。因此，在阶段间无人类检查的情况下自主演化功能，对当前编码智能体仍是重大挑战。在腾讯，该流水线将内部评估扩展到这一设置，并指导腾讯大语言模型家族混元的开发。

2610.37624.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
2610.37624.authors: Anouar Imel , Imad Charradi , Abderrahman Sghir , Khalil El Khammar
2610.37624.categories_text: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI) ; Computation and Language (cs.CL); Multiagent Systems (cs.MA); Social and Information Networks (cs.SI)
2610.37624.abstract_en: When an LLM group's discussion is compressed into a short memory for a final decision maker, what should the memory keep? Two natural heuristics keep the rarest claims or the claims relevant to the decision criteria. On hidden-profile tasks both look attractive, because how widely a fact is held is confounded with whether it helps. We introduce CrossProfile, a diagnostic benchmark of 60 templates with automatically verified answer keys, in which the ownership of supporting, decoy, and irrelevant facts is crossed while their text is held fixed (480 tasks). Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and two DeepSeek models, both heuristics fail in predictable places. Selecting by relevance readmits decoys, because decoys are on topic: even a perfect relevance filter loses 23 to 31 points to rarest-first selection in the classic hidden-profile configuration. Rarest-first selection is no better than random selection on average and wins only where the rare facts happen to be the useful ones. In both cases accuracy follows the balance of evidence the memory keeps, not the policy that kept it. The decision model adds a third failure, a form of social proof: it gives extra weight to facts attributed to many agents. Removing the attribution tags, or reassigning them at random with line order fixed, raises accuracy in the classic configuration by 13 to 24 points. In natural discussions the evidence is lost before any memory acts: the complete transcript yields lower accuracy than no notes at all.
2610.37624.affiliation: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China; Xidian University; Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics; Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology
2610.37624.update_target: Memory selection and attribution effects on group decisions
2610.37624.mechanism_en: CrossProfile crosses ownership of fixed supporting/decoy/irrelevant facts with verified answers. Attribution removal/randomization holds text and line order fixed to test social-proof effects.
2610.37624.result_en: Across 480 tasks, relevance selection can lose 23–31 points to rarest-first in the classic configuration; rarest-first is no better than random on average. Removing attribution raises accuracy 13–24 points.
2610.37624.boundary_en: Rare or relevant is not equivalent to decision-supporting. Controlled hidden-profile tasks and natural discussion have different loss mechanisms; a memory heuristic cannot recover evidence never expressed.
2610.37624.abstract_zh: 当 LLM 群体讨论被压缩为供最终决策者使用的短记忆时，应保留什么？两种自然启发式分别保留最稀有主张，或与决策标准相关的主张。在隐藏画像任务上，两者看起来都很有吸引力，因为事实被多少人持有，与它是否有帮助相混杂。我们提出 CrossProfile，一个诊断基准，包含 60 个模板和自动验证答案；在事实文本固定的情况下，交叉改变支持、诱饵和无关事实的持有归属，形成 480 个任务。在 Qwen2.5-7B、Llama-3.1-8B 及两个 DeepSeek 模型上，两种启发式都在可预测的位置失败。按相关性选择会重新引入诱饵，因为诱饵也切合主题：即使完美相关性过滤器，在经典隐藏画像配置中，也比最稀有优先选择低 23—31 个点。最稀有优先平均不比随机选择好，只在稀有事实恰巧有用时获胜。两种情况下，准确率都随记忆保留的证据平衡而变化，而不是随保留策略变化。决策模型还增加第三种失败，即一种社会认同效应：它给被归属于许多智能体的事实额外权重。删除归属标签，或在行序固定时随机重分配标签，可将经典配置的准确率提高 13—24 个点。在自然讨论中，证据在任何记忆发挥作用前就已丢失：完整讨论文本的准确率比完全没有笔记还低。

2610.37649.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
2610.37649.authors: Zhen Yang , Wen Wang , Xander Xu , Ying-Cong Chen
2610.37649.categories_text: Computation and Language (cs.CL) ; Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Multiagent Systems (cs.MA)
2610.37649.abstract_en: Scientific discovery often begins with an unexpected observation that prompts a new research question. In a world with altered physical laws, can large language models (LLMs) notice unexpected behavior, such as heavier objects falling more slowly, and discover the law through experiments without being told what to investigate? To evaluate this ability, we introduce LongChang, an automated framework that creates simulated worlds with altered physics, where one or more laws differ from ordinary physics. The evaluated LLMs act as explorers, manipulating objects and building tools to investigate their own questions without research tasks or hints about these laws. Separate LLM agents generate and review scenes, review tool designs, and evaluate reports for correctness and experimental support using the altered physical laws and exploration records. These records guide scene evolution for further exploration, allowing the full cycle to run without human intervention. Among 12 LLMs, GPT-6-Astra achieves a discovery rate of 16.7%, while the other 11 score 0%. The exploration records reveal uninvestigated anomalies and only partial identification of the altered physical laws.
2610.37649.affiliation: HKUST (Guangzhou); ZJU; Alibaba Group; HKUST (as listed)
2610.37649.update_target: Evaluation of free scientific exploration and evidence-guided scene evolution
2610.37649.mechanism_en: Explorers manipulate altered-physics worlds and design tools without a research question or hints. Separate model agents generate/review scenes and assess reports using the hidden laws and execution records.
2610.37649.result_en: Of twelve evaluated LLMs, GPT-6-Astra reaches 16.7% discovery while the other eleven score 0%; logs reveal unexplored anomalies and partial law identification.
2610.37649.boundary_en: These are authored simulated laws with model-based review, not discoveries of unknown real-world physics. Autonomous environment evolution does not alone prove that the explorer becomes a better scientist.
2610.37649.abstract_zh: 科学发现通常始于意外观测，由此提出新的研究问题。在物理规律被改变的世界里，大语言模型（LLM）能否在没有被告知应研究什么的情况下，注意到重物下落更慢等意外现象，并通过实验发现规律？为评估这种能力，我们提出 LongChang，一个创建改变物理规律的模拟世界的自动框架，其中一条或多条规律不同于普通物理。被评估 LLM 充当探索者，操控物体、构建工具，研究自己提出的问题，不提供研究任务或有关规律的提示。独立 LLM 智能体生成和审查场景、审查工具设计，并利用改变后的物理规律及探索记录，评估报告的正确性和实验支持。这些记录指导场景演化，以供进一步探索，使完整循环无需人工干预运行。在 12 个 LLM 中，GPT-6-Astra 的发现率为 16.7%，另外 11 个为 0%。探索记录揭示，存在未被研究的异常，对改变后的物理规律也仅有部分识别。
